A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BCNP research despite the revised title. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on two-variable posterior sampling, synthetic causal models, and Syntren, including additional results and equal-width comparisons in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results for BCNP All Data across the existing synthetic evaluation settings.

M1.justification: The transformer encoder, permutation/Bernoulli decoder, DAG sampling procedure, and training objective are unchanged. BCNP All Data uses the existing method with a different training mixture.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same two-variable Gaussian task, Linear/NeuralNet/GPCDE synthetic families with ER20/40/60 graphs, and Syntren datasets. Joint training combines existing coverage without adding a dataset family or test scenario.

E2.justification: DiBS, BayesDAG, AVICI, and CSIvA remain in the corresponding comparisons. The additional BCNP All Data rows represent a training configuration of the proposed method; the earlier BCNP configurations remain in the appendix.

E3.justification: The synthetic evaluation adds one BCNP model trained jointly across all three function families and graph densities, extending v1's per-family density mixtures. Existing sample sizes, preprocessing, model settings, and metric definitions are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 extends the training-mixture analysis to examine whether one model can serve all function families and densities. The existing two-variable posterior check and equal-width controls are retained.

E5.justification: The added rows follow the existing mean-and-uncertainty reporting convention. Neither version introduces different seed information, repeated-run counts, significance tests, or uncertainty estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds BCNP All Data results to Tables 7–15, including GPCDE ER60 AUC 0.77 ± 0.01 and expected edge F1 0.25 ± 0.01. All earlier configuration scores remain unchanged in the appendix. The main ER60 table highlights the new training configuration instead of BCNP ER20-60; this is additional evidence under different training conditions.

T1.justification: The causal-model definitions, posterior and loss derivations, permutation-equivariance reasoning, and appendix mathematics are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim full-posterior approximation with acyclic sampling, edge dependencies, and permutation equivariance, together with strong empirical performance. The contribution statements and conclusion retain the same scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 extends the interpretation that mixture training mitigates misspecification from within-family graph-density mixtures to joint training across function families. Appendix C.1 explicitly endorses this broader strategy. Section 5's distribution-mismatch and interventional-data limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code link named CausalStructureNeuralProcess and explicitly distinguishes the training distributions associated with the BCNP row labels in Appendix C.1. The existing implementation and hyperparameter details are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The abstract now characterizes earlier meta-learning work as posterior estimation rather than maximum-a-posteriori graph estimation, modestly adjusting its positioning. The cited works and detailed related-work discussion remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds 'Transformer' to the title, lightly rewrites the abstract, converts contribution bullets to inline enumeration, and updates publication and citation styling. Appendix C is reorganized around the relocated two-variable results; most prose and section ordering remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts ICLR formatting, moves v1's Table 6 into the main paper as Table 3, and adds All Data rows to existing result tables. Both figures are retained. Table 9 changes its heading to 'Neg. Log Prob.' despite retaining negative log-probability values and the original metric definition.

improvement.justification: The joint-training comparison adds useful evidence about deploying one BCNP model across the existing synthetic families, while the new code link improves reproducibility information. Original results and methodological details are preserved. These modest gains outweigh the inconsistent Table 9 heading and the overly broad no-performance-loss interpretation, which is not uniform across metrics and settings such as NeuralNet ER40 in Table 11.
